courseTitle: Ionic - Build iOS, Android & Web Apps with Ionic & Angular

cues.en: Let's output some place data and let's do that in our discover area, in the place detail component
which is that page here. There we're outputting the description and then we have the book button.
Now wouldn't it be nice if we also saw a preview of the place here and the address? So let's add a new
ion-row here with an ion-column and that column will receive the same sizing as my other columns
do, like this and I'll also add the padding attribute utility attribute here and now in that column, I
want to output my address. So for that, I'll add a new paragraph in here and then I'll output place location
and now there, we should have an address field because if we check our location modal, our place location
modal has an address field and that just is the location we store in a place.
Now let me copy that and let's add another ion-row and in there, I want to output an ion-img and that
ion-img here of course will now be bound to place location
and then if we check our modal again, we have that static map imageUrl, so it's that static map imageUrl
which I target here,
so that we also output an image of that location.
Now for the proper styling, I'll give this a class of location image here
and therefore in the place-detail.page.scss file, we can style location image and give this a
width of 100%, a height of let's say 25rem and a max height of 30vh and an object fit of
cover so that this hopefully looks good. Let's save this and let's give it a try as this reloads,
yes here's our address and here's our map preview. Now there is some room for improvement.
First of all, I want to center my address text, so let me add text center here and then there is a little
bit too much padding.
So on this page, I'll actually target my paragraphs and I'll remove the margin,
sorry I mean margin, not padding,
so there is less space between these paragraphs.
So now as this reloads, this looks way better.
And then there is our map, which is of course nice but I actually don't want to have padding around that
map,
so here I'll remove the padding on that column that holds the image so that this takes a full width here,
there still is some padding and that can be avoided by explicitly adding no padding here to remove that
default padding that grid columns have otherwise.
And now this takes the full width which looks nicer in my opinion, also doesn't look too bad here on
a desktop device, though of course you could consider adding some borders or drop shadows around the
image and the map here but it'll do for now here, don't want to turn this into a CSS course. What I
want to add though is that if we click that image here, that we open that modal again where we can't pick
a new place of course but where we can scroll around to see what's around that area and so on.
